open_points.subject: Token-list re-read failure handling between `installation` and `surface`
open_points.text: `installation` owns "the re-read of the token list on every request ... with the three checks of A16 rule 2"; `surface` owns "A16: ... token comparison in constant time ..."
open_points.question: When A16 rule 2 re-read fails, which module owns and persists the "refuse every request (including owner) with the same token refusal" state, and how is that enforced on each request without duplicating A16 logic?
options: `installation` returns an explicit "token list invalid/refuse-all" result and `surface` only maps it to the one refusal
`surface` re-implements A16 rule 2 checks and refusal behavior itself, with `installation` only reading raw config bytes
open_points.default_guess: Make `installation` own the re-read outcome state and expose a single "token check context" result that `surface` consumes.

open_points.subject: Startup spool cleanup responsibility (`store.open_store` vs `runs.recover_running_runs`)
open_points.text: `store` owns "start-time removal of temporary files, and removal of the spools `runs` names"; start order says `store.open_store` runs before `runs.recover_running_runs`, and `runs.recover_running_runs` "first names to `store.remove_run_spool` every ended run that no longer keeps its spool"
open_points.question: At startup, who is responsible for determining which ended runs' spool directories must be removed under A14/A18: `store.open_store` independently, or only `runs.recover_running_runs` via explicit naming?
options: `store.open_store` scans DB/files and removes eligible ended-run spools on its own
Only `runs.recover_running_runs` decides eligibility and calls `store.remove_run_spool`; `store.open_store` removes only temp files
open_points.default_guess: Have `runs.recover_running_runs` decide eligibility and call `store.remove_run_spool`; keep `store.open_store` to temp-file cleanup only.

open_points.subject: Effect-class comparison ownership (`flows` vs `effects`)
open_points.text: "every comparison goes through ... or, for effect classes, the order of `EFFECT_CLASSES` read by `flows` alone"
open_points.question: How should `effects` implement A10 class-dependent behavior (`draft-write` special case, `destructive` cannot be granted, approval-required classes) if effect-class comparison/order is said to be read by `flows` alone?
options: Allow `effects` to read `EFFECT_CLASSES` (or a helper) directly for all class checks
Keep `flows` as sole effect-class reader and expose helper decisions to `effects`
open_points.default_guess: Let `effects` read a shared effect-class helper/constant directly, because A10 decisions are owned there.
